messages.author: 5e7e51497bbaca60
messages.subject: Non-Significant Variance in SEM and bootstrapping does not work
parts:
Hello there, 

for my Master thesis I need to do an SEM.
This is my model so far:

sem_fixed_var <- '
        # Measurement model
        wfomo_f1 =~ wfomo1 + wfomo2 + wfomo3 + wfomo4 + wfomo5
        wfomo_f2 =~ wfomo6 + wfomo7 + wfomo8 + wfomo9 + wfomo10
        preference_f1 =~ preference1 + preference2 + preference3 + preference4
        BSH_f1 =~ BSH1 + BSH2 + BSH3 + BSH4 + BSH5 + BSH6 + BSH7 + BSH8
        abschalten_f1 =~ abschalten1 + abschalten2 + abschalten3 + abschalten4
       
        # wfomo is a second order factor
        wfomo_f =~ wfomo_f1 + wfomo_f2
       
        # Fix the variance of the higher order factor to 1
        wfomo_f ~~ 1*wfomo_f
       
        # Item correlations
        wfomo9 ~~ wfomo10
        abschalten1 ~~ abschalten2
        BSH1 ~~ BSH6
        BSH7 ~~ BSH8
        BSH3 ~~ BSH8
        wfomo2 ~~ wfomo5
        BSH1 ~~ BSH4
        BSH5 ~~ BSH7
        BSH1 ~~ BSH3
        preference1 ~~ preference3
        wfomo5 ~~ wfomo9
       
        # Direct effects
        preference_f1 ~ a1*wfomo_f
        BSH_f1 ~ a2*wfomo_f + b1*preference_f1
        abschalten_f1 ~ a3*wfomo_f + b2*BSH_f1
       
        # Indirect effects
        indirect_on_bsh := a1 * b1  # wfomo -> preference -> bsh
        indirect_on_detachment := a2 * b2  # wfomo -> bsh -> detachment
       
        # Total effects
        total_bsh := a2 + (a1 * b1)  # Direct effect + indirect effect through preference
        total_detachment := a3 + (a2 * b2) + (a1 * b1 * b2)  # Direct effect + indirect effect through bsh + indirect effect through preference and bsh
'

My problems are: Bootstrapping does not work, how could that be?
I used Santorra-Bentler correction instead but I would prefer bootstrapping to get robust results.

The bigger problem: wfomo_f1 seems to be an issue. Why is the variance not significant? The rsquares for the items range from 0.482 to 0.801

What could I do about that, are there any mistakes in my model specification?

Thank you so much for your help!

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: Non-Significant Variance in SEM and bootstrapping does not work
parts:
On Tue, 9 Jul 2024 at 02:16, 'Greta Ueltzen' via lavaan <lav...@googlegroups.com> wrote:
When I use bootsrapping for the model estimation, I get the follwing warning:
In lav_model_nvcov_bootstrap(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats, : lavaan WARNING: 227 bootstrap runs resulted in nonadmissible solutions.

I used the default with 1000 runs, I am not sure how to interpret the warning, I do get results out of this

I'd be a bit worried about my model. It looks like you're right on the edge of acceptability. A non-admissible solution means that Lavaan found an answer but the answer that it found can't exist in the real world (e.g. a negative variance).  This is normally a sign that your model is misspecified. If bootstrap resamples have a problem, it means that you are very close to an unacceptable model. Maybe you can say "Well, more than 3/4 of the models were acceptable, so I'll go for it", maybe you can add a constraint, for example, in a growth model, you sometimes need to fix the variance of a slope to zero, which means that there is no variance in the slope - this could be OK, everyone has the same slope.  Maybe, as Terrence says about, use Satorra-Bentler - why do you need to bootstrap?

Jeremy
